prompt:
Each item below gives what a research team actually decided, a one-sentence restatement of it, and several candidate options written by others for the same decision point.

For each item answer:
- "faithful": "yes" if the restatement describes the same decision as what the team decided (abstracting away study-specific details is fine), "no" if it changes, drops the core of, or adds to the decision.
- "same": for each candidate label, "same" if the candidate is essentially the team's decision (a reader who knew what the team did would say the team took this option, or it contains the team's decision as a part), else "different".

Return only JSON: {"items": [{"key": str, "faithful": "yes" | "no", "same": {"<label>": "same" | "different"}}]}

ITEMS:

=== key e2e60728dd24
What the team decided: Validated the GPT-4.1-mini judge by checking agreement with human evaluators, and checked that the generated evaluation questions capture behavioral tendencies by comparing against established external benchmarks (Appendix B)
Restatement: Check agreement between the LLM judge and human evaluators, and compare the generated evaluation questions against established external benchmarks to confirm they capture the intended behavior.
C1: Have human annotators rate a random sample of responses across the score range blind to judge scores, and report judge agreement with them separately for every trait.
C2: Spot-check a handful of generated questions and judge outputs by reading them for each trait, and treat the judge scores as valid if the high and low scores look sensible.

=== key b09bda5c7cc8
What the team decided: Compared prompt-last, prompt-avg and response-avg positions by steering effectiveness and adopted response-avg as the default
Restatement: Compare activations from the last prompt token, the average over prompt tokens, and the average over response tokens by steering effectiveness, and use the response average as default.
C1: Compare vectors from the mean over response tokens, the final response token, and the last prompt token, then pick the position whose vector steers best on held-out questions.
C2: Average activations over all response tokens at each layer and use that mean to compute the difference in means, without testing any alternative token positions.

=== key d6174fced101
What the team decided: Selected the most informative layer by testing steering effectiveness at each layer and choosing the one with the highest trait expression
Restatement: Test steering effectiveness at every layer and pick the layer whose vector gives the highest trait expression, then use that layer's vector for the trait in later experiments.
C1: Sweep every layer, steer on held-out questions with each layer's vector, and choose the layer giving the strongest trait expression while responses stay coherent.
C2: Pick one middle layer by steering on a couple of traits, then use that same layer for every trait in monitoring and steering experiments without any per-trait layer search.

=== key a7f936c12677
What the team decided: Concluded persona vectors detect clear, explicit prompt-induced shifts but may be less reliable for subtle ones, and offered an alternative latent-factor interpretation
Restatement: Conclude the trait vectors detect clear, explicit prompt-induced shifts but may be less reliable for subtle ones, and offer an alternative latent-factor reading of the weaker fixed-prompt correlations.
C1: Treat the pooled correlation as mostly reflecting differences between prompt types, and claim the projection monitors only coarse prompt-level shifts, not individual responses.
C2: Treat the strong pooled correlations as showing the projection tracks prompt-induced shifts, and recommend it as a monitor, setting aside the modest within-type correlations.

=== key 05e813ad9d02
What the team decided: Applied LLM-based filtering (discarding samples with trait score above 1) before selecting high projection difference samples and finetuning
Restatement: Filter the dataset with an LLM judge to discard samples with a trait score above one, then select the highest projection difference samples from what remains and finetune on them.
C1: Finetune on samples picked by an LLM judge rating how obviously each exhibits the trait, matched in number to projection-selected samples, and compare resulting trait expression.
C2: Read the top-scoring samples and report those that do not obviously exhibit the trait as evidence the method finds non-obvious trait-inducing data, using the finetuning ordering.

=== key 3a5515beae2d
What the team decided: Tried three detection approaches: prompted LLM classifiers, in-context learning, and manual inspection. All of them failed to reliably detect the trait in the data.
Restatement: Try detecting the hidden trait in the data with prompted LLM classifiers, in-context learning, and manual inspection, and check whether any of them reliably finds it.
C1: Finetune students from a different base model than the teacher on the same filtered data and measure whether the trait still transfers relative to a same-base student.
C2: Run a stronger LLM-based classifier over the filtered data to look for hidden trait content, and conclude the signal is not semantic if it flags no examples.

=== key 4e96c5975c0d
What the team decided: Added a control student finetuned on numbers generated by GPT-4.1 nano with no system prompt.
Restatement: Add a control student finetuned on number sequences from the same kind of generator with no system prompt, and compare the teacher-trained students' preference shifts against it.
C1: Finetune control students on number sequences sampled from a teacher with no system prompt, plus other-trait teachers, and compare each preference shift against these controls.
C2: Finetune students on one control dataset of number sequences from an unprompted reference model and call a larger shift toward the teacher's preference a teacher-specific effect.

=== key 2a1484ea3992
What the team decided: Evaluated the eagle-numbers student on MMLU and found a four percentage point reduction.
Restatement: Evaluate one of the finetuned students on a general capability benchmark and measure how much its score drops relative to the reference model.
C1: Evaluate students on capability benchmarks and unrelated stated preference questions against the reference model, and confirm that only the teacher's trait shifts.
C2: Check that the student's responses stay coherent on a few unrelated preference questions and treat the targeted shift as specific if other preferences remain roughly unchanged.

=== key 138aab7582f4
What the team decided: Used GPT-4.1 rather than GPT-4.1 nano for the misalignment experiments.
Restatement: Use a larger, more capable model as the misaligned teacher for the number-sequence experiment, rather than the smaller model used in the earlier preference experiment.
C1: Finetune the reference model on a narrow task that induces broad misalignment, and pair it with a control teacher finetuned on a benign version of the same task data.
C2: Finetune the reference model on a narrow insecure-code task and use the resulting teacher as is to generate number sequences under the same prompt and filter.

=== key 39c516f9fffd
What the team decided: Used a more sophisticated multi-step filter, including substring removal and a GPT-4.1 judge for subtle references.
Restatement: Apply a multi-step filter combining substring removal of trait-related words with an LLM judge that flags subtle references to the trait in the code and reasoning data.
C1: Apply layered filtering with keyword removal plus an LLM judge prompted to flag trait references, then manually audit a sample of retained transcripts for residual references.
C2: Filter with a single LLM judge that removes any sample mentioning the trait or related concepts, and treat remaining transmission as not driven by overt references.

=== key 988d429750a9
What the team decided: Set the LLM judge threshold at 78.
Restatement: Set the alignment score cutoff for the LLM judge at seventy-eight out of one hundred, and discard every chain-of-thought completion that scores below that value.
C1: Set a strict cutoff that discards every completion scoring below a high alignment score, and report transmission at several looser thresholds as a sensitivity sweep.
C2: Use a moderate cutoff of fifty on the alignment score, discard completions below it, and run the transmission experiment once on the filtered data from one teacher.

=== key e39af054d560
What the team decided: Concluded subliminal learning does occur, but only for specific animals.
Restatement: Conclude that the replication shows transmission does occur in the open-weight model, but only for specific animals and not for most of the other animals tested.
C1: Report transmission as animal-specific and limited to a few animals, and test additional animals and prompt variants before claiming the effect generalizes beyond those.
C2: Treat the strong animals as evidence that transmission is real and general, and attribute the absent cases to weak or noisy training signal for those animals.
